elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Every Customer-payable formula survives verbatim: 14.2.1/14.2.2/14.2.5.2 and 14.2.7 require PB to pay "three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs", 14.2.6 and 14.2.8.1 require "one hundred fifty percent (150%)", 14.2.9 requires "all Development Costs", and 14.2.10 requires Development Costs "plus interest at the annual rate of twenty-five percent (25%)". The inserted sentence caps rather than eliminates, so the preferred no-LD outcome is not reached.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The new sentence says "the sole liquidated amount payable by PB ... is an early-termination fee not exceeding three months of Development Costs", but "liquidated amount" is undefined and each retained formula is expressly framed as consideration "in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results" \u2014 i.e. as purchase price, not as a liquidated amount. SFJ can therefore argue the 300%/150% payments fall outside the cap entirely, leaving them payable in full alongside the new fee.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is measured as "three months of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ" \u2014 SFJ's spend, not fees paid or payable by PB \u2014 and no monthly run-rate is defined anywhere (Development Costs is defined as an aggregate of "all internal and external costs incurred or paid by SFJ or PB"). The amount is therefore uncomputable: the drafter must state the measurement basis, e.g. "an amount equal to three (3) times the average monthly Development Costs incurred during the twelve (12) months preceding the effective date of termination".

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The override reaches only "anything to the contrary in this Section 14.2", yet the retained subsections continue to impose the 300%/150%/100% payments and the 25% annual interest in 14.2.10 in operative terms, and 14.2.1's cumulative right to "pursue remedies it may have at law or equity ... including the right to seek damages" is untouched. The result is an internally inconsistent clause in which the retained formulas contradict the asserted sole amount; the drafter must delete or conform each of 14.2.1, 14.2.2, 14.2.5.2, 14.2.6, 14.2.7, 14.2.8.1, 14.2.9 and 14.2.10, or expressly deem those payments to be the capped early-termination fee.

reasons: Position-incomplete at both levels: the insertion adds a cap sentence but deletes or conforms none of the eight retained Customer-payable termination formulas, so no level is fully met.

Internal inconsistency: retained 14.2.1\u201314.2.10 expressly obligate PB to pay 300%/150%/100% of Development Costs (plus 25% interest under 14.2.10) while the new sentence asserts a single capped early-termination fee; a contradictory retained sentence defeats preservation of intent.

Undefined trigger/term: "liquidated amount" is undefined and the retained payments are characterised as purchase consideration for the Trial Data Package, so the cap may not bite on them at all. Add a deeming provision, e.g. "each amount payable by PB under Sections 14.2.1 through 14.2.10 constitutes a liquidated amount and is superseded by this Section".

Uncomputable cap base: "three months of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ" has no defined monthly rate and is measured against SFJ's spend rather than fees paid or payable by PB; specify an average-monthly multiplier and a Customer-fee base.

Minimality is satisfied on its face \u2014 the edit is a single concise insertion, deletes nothing, and adds no survival tail, procedure or extra remedy outside the LD checklist \u2014 but that economy is what leaves the retained formulas unreconciled.
